title: Sign-out and administrative revoke both invalidate on the server
asA: operator who wants sign-out to actually mean the session is gone
iWant: POST /logout to invalidate the session server-side and revocation-by-principal to end every session for that principal
soThat: a leaked cookie stops working the moment I have signed out or the moment an administrator revokes me

acceptanceCriteria.description: POST /logout invalidates the server-side session record for the presented handle and returns a response that clears the session cookie on the browser.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an authenticated request with a valid session cookie
acceptanceCriteria.then: the session record for that handle is deleted from the store, and the response carries a Set-Cookie header clearing the session cookie (Max-Age=0 or an expiry in the past)

acceptanceCriteria.description: After POST /logout, a subsequent request presenting the same handle is treated as unauthenticated.
acceptanceCriteria.given: POST /logout has completed for a session S
acceptanceCriteria.when: a subsequent authenticated request is made using S's handle
acceptanceCriteria.then: the server treats the request as unauthenticated (redirects to /login or returns 401 per the surface's convention) and does not resurrect the session

acceptanceCriteria.description: The session manager exposes a revokeAllForPrincipal(principalId) operation that invalidates every unexpired session for that principal in one call.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a principal with N unexpired sessions in the store
acceptanceCriteria.when: revokeAllForPrincipal is invoked with that principal id
acceptanceCriteria.then: the store's session count for that principal drops to zero and every previously issued handle for that principal fails validation on the next request
